Cantankerous

kan-TANG-ker-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Cantankerous is habitually bad-tempered, argumentative, and difficult to work or get along with.

The cantankerous committee chair objected to every proposal at the meeting, no matter how small or reasonable.

Worked Example

Nobody wanted to sit near the cantankerous passenger who complained about the temperature, the snacks, and the flight attendant's tone, all within the first ten minutes.

Cantankerous describes an ongoing pattern of grumbling and picking fights, not just one bad mood -- it's a personality that's hard to satisfy.

How Cantankerous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

irritable

irritable: easily annoyed

quarrelsome

quarrelsome: eager to argue or fight

Antonyms

genial

genial: warmly friendly and pleasant

agreeable

agreeable: pleasant and willing to cooperate

How Strong Is It? — irritable → cantankerous → hostile

irritable vs. cantankerous

irritable vs. cantankerous: Being irritable is milder and more temporary -- someone irritable might just be having a rough day, not a lifelong pattern.

hostile vs. cantankerous

hostile vs. cantankerous: Hostile goes further than cantankerous, suggesting open unfriendliness or even aggression, not just grumbling and arguing.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — cantanker-

root — cantanker-: likely a blend of words meaning 'strife' and 'bitterness' (Middle English, origin disputed)

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: full of, having the quality of (Latin (-osus))

Put it together

Put it together: Cantankerous has a disputed history -- word historians suspect a blend of an old word for 'strife' (contek) with rancorous ('bitter and resentful'). Its one certain piece is the ending -ous ('full of'), describing someone full of quarrelsome ill temper.

Use the root in a new word: rancorous

Use the root in a new word: rancorous: Rancorous describes bitter, long-lasting resentment -- word historians think it may be one of the two words blended together to form cantankerous.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Cantankerous almost always paints a fond, slightly humorous picture -- think of the classic grumpy-but-familiar neighbor or relative -- rather than describing someone genuinely dangerous or cruel.
